properties.name: A comparison says when its two sides were written by different builds
properties.statement: When two design records being compared were written by different reflow2 builds, the comparison discloses that and says that property-only differences may be attributable to the build change rather than to anything anybody decided. Every export already carries `reflow2_version` in its stamp, so the input exists and is not read. THIS IS DISCLOSURE, NOT A THRESHOLD, and the distinction is the requirement: nothing is suppressed, reweighted or hidden — the reader is told what could confound their reading, the way `propose_heal` discloses that the alphabet chose a merge survivor. Tuning severity until phantom findings fall below a cut-off is explicitly NOT this, because it silences true and false findings at the same rate. THE EVIDENCE IS TWO INCIDENTS, NOT AN ARGUMENT: 2026-08-08 and 2026-08-10 were both cross-build comparisons, both produced a confident false data-loss claim written into a PR body, and neither reader could see the confound (`fact:bl-198-cost-measured-twice-in-both-directions`). It is also what step 1 does not fix — suppressing defaults cleans the steady state and moves the disagreement to the version transition, which every upgrading consumer meets once.
